outcome.answer:
Several papers address multimodal LLM decoding strategies. The closest matches are training-free decoding methods for diffusion-based multimodal language models: IGFD ranks candidates by confidence, neighborhood uncertainty, and commitment risk to favor semantic anchors over fragile structural tokens [1]; VRCD prioritizes visually complementary positions to reduce visual redundancy among jointly committed tokens [2]; and CACD scores masked positions using confidence plus neighbor proximity to improve coherence and reduce hallucination in long-form outputs [3].

If you want broader decoding methods for multimodal/vision-language models, the survey summarizes token-level, sequence-level, and parallel generation approaches and notes open challenges [5]. Other supplied papers focus on hallucination mitigation rather than decoding order specifically [4, 9].
